stories.title: The Wobbly Start
stories.text:
Aisha stood at the top of the park slope with her new bike. Dad had taken off the training wheels that morning. The smell of [ha|warm kaya toast] drifted from the café nearby. [x1|A jogger ran past with a small dog.] Below her, [hb|the long, empty path] stretched toward the playground. Her hands shook on the handlebars. [hc|Her blue swimming goggles] dangled from the bag on her back.

"I will fall," she whispered.

"Maybe," said Dad. "Then you try again."

Aisha pushed off. The bike wobbled left and right. [x2|The wind blew her hair across her face.] She fell onto the grass. [la|She laughed, brushed off her knees and climbed back on.] [lb|Her tummy felt tiny and fluttery,] but she kept pedalling. "[lc|Brave is feeling scared and trying anyway,]" she told herself, and she rode all the way to the playground.

areas.memory: Last year, Aisha dropped an egg while helping Grandma cook. Grandma laughed and said, "Pick it up and try again."
areas.wh: The smell of kaya toast is the same smell as in Grandma's kitchen.
areas.wr: Good: a smell is a strong hook, but the memory is about a small kitchen mistake, so it helps less than the goggles.
areas.wl: Falling, laughing and trying again is the same action as dropping the egg and trying again.

areas.memory: On her first day of Primary 1, Aisha walked down a long, empty corridor alone. Her tummy felt tiny and fluttery.
areas.wh: A long, empty path looks like the long, empty corridor.
areas.wr: Workable: a place is a weak hook because many places look alike, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: The fluttery tummy is the same feeling in both scenes.

areas.memory: Last year, Aisha was afraid to jump into the pool. Her coach said, "Brave is feeling scared and trying anyway." Then she jumped.
areas.wh: The goggles are the same personal object she wore at the pool.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object, noticed when she is most afraid. The memory gives her the exact words she needs.
areas.wl: She repeats her coach's words, so the lesson carries into the ending.

decoys.x1: A jogger and a dog are not in any memory. Nothing connects them to Aisha's fear.
decoys.x2: The wind is only weather here. No memory makes it matter.

stories.title: The New Boy
stories.text:
The school canteen was loud and busy. [ha|Trays clattered and children shouted.] [x1|A teacher walked by with a big water bottle.] Ravi carried his lunch to his usual table. Then he saw the new boy, Kai, sitting alone. Kai held [hb|a red lunchbox with a dented lid] but did not open it. The smell of [hc|hot curry puffs] came from the stall behind them. Ravi stood still for a moment.

He walked over, his heart beating fast. [x2|The clock above the stall said 10.30.] Kai's shoulders were hunched, and he looked [la|small and lost in the noisy room.] "[lb|Come sit with us!]" Ravi said, and he smiled. Kai's face brightened. Ravi opened his lunch and [lc|shared a curry puff with him.] Soon the two boys were laughing together.

areas.memory: In his first week of Primary 1, Ravi stood alone in the canteen. His tray shook and he felt small and lost.
areas.wh: A noisy canteen is the place where Ravi once felt lost.
areas.wr: Workable: any canteen is noisy, so the place alone is a weak hook.
areas.wl: Kai feels small and lost, just as Ravi once did.

areas.memory: In Primary 1, Ravi carried a red lunchbox with a dented lid. A girl named Priya saw him alone and said, "Come sit with us!"
areas.wh: The dented red lunchbox looks just like the one Ravi carried that day.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object that appears just as Ravi decides what to do. Priya's words become his words.
areas.wl: Ravi says Priya's words to Kai.

areas.memory: Ravi's mum always packed extra curry puffs. She said, "Food tastes better when it is shared."
areas.wh: The smell of curry puffs reminds Ravi of his mum's lunchbox.
areas.wr: Good: a smell is a strong hook, but Kai is lonely, not hungry, so the memory is less central.
areas.wl: Sharing a curry puff is the same action as sharing food in the memory.

decoys.x1: A teacher with a water bottle plays no part in any memory.
decoys.x2: The clock only tells the time. It does not remind Ravi of anything.

stories.title: The Piano Recital
stories.text:
Priya waited in the school hall for her turn at the piano recital. [ha|The silver star clip in her hair] felt cool against her head. [x1|A boy in the front row yawned loudly.] Her name was called. Priya walked towards [hb|the dark side of the stage,] and her legs felt wobbly. She sat down and looked at the keys. [hc|The slow, steady tick of the metronome] filled the quiet hall. Her hands began to shake.

Priya's fingers found the clip. [la|She touched the star and breathed in slowly.] Her cheeks burned hot, [lb|and she felt embarrassed in front of everyone.] [x2|A fan whirred above the stage.] "[lc|Slow and steady,]" she whispered. Then she began to play, and the music flowed.

areas.memory: On the night of her first recital, Grandma pinned a silver star clip in Priya's hair. She said, "When your hands shake, touch the star and breathe in slowly."
areas.wh: Grandma pinned this very clip in Priya's hair before her first recital.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object, noticed just before the problem peaks. The memory gives her something to do.
areas.wl: Touching the star and breathing slowly is the same action Grandma taught.

areas.memory: At her nursery concert, Priya went the wrong way backstage. She was lost in the dark and her cheeks burned with embarrassment.
areas.wh: A dark backstage is like the dark backstage at her nursery concert.
areas.wr: Workable: dark places are common, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Embarrassment is the same feeling in both scenes.

areas.memory: Every evening, Dad counted along with the metronome as Priya practised. He would say, "Slow and steady wins the song."
areas.wh: Dad counted with the metronome whenever she practised.
areas.wr: Good: a sound is a strong hook and fits the lesson, but it comes after the fear has already started.
areas.wl: Priya whispers Dad's words to herself.

decoys.x1: A boy yawning has nothing to do with Priya's memories.
decoys.x2: A fan is background noise. No memory is tied to it.

stories.title: The Extra Change
stories.text:
On Sunday, Jia Hao went to the hawker centre to buy breakfast for his family. The smell of [ha|fish soup] filled the air. [x1|A cat slept under a plastic chair.] He joined [hb|the long queue at the drinks stall] and waited. At last, he paid with a ten-dollar note and held his [hc|dad's old red coin purse] open. The uncle gave him the change quickly. Jia Hao walked to a table and sat down.

[la|He counted the coins in his hand.] There was an extra five dollars! The uncle had made a mistake. [x2|A baby cried at the next table.] Jia Hao's [lb|ears felt hot with shame] as he thought about keeping it. "[lc|Honest is what you do when no one is watching,]" he told himself. He ran back and gave the money to the uncle. The uncle smiled and gave him a free packet of kaya toast.

areas.memory: Every Sunday, Dad bought fish soup and let Jia Hao pay. Dad always said, "Count your change before you leave."
areas.wh: Fish soup was Dad's Sunday breakfast, when he taught Jia Hao about change.
areas.wr: Good: a smell is a strong hook, but the memory only teaches counting, not what to do with extra money.
areas.wl: Counting the coins is the same action Dad taught.

areas.memory: Once, Jia Hao pushed into a long queue. The auntie behind him looked hurt, and he felt hot with shame.
areas.wh: A long queue is like the queue where Jia Hao once pushed in.
areas.wr: Workable: queues are everywhere, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Shame is the same feeling in both scenes.

areas.memory: When Jia Hao was seven, Dad gave him his old red coin purse. Dad said, "Honest is what you do when no one is watching."
areas.wh: Dad gave Jia Hao this very coin purse and spoke these words.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object noticed right at his choice. The memory gives him the words that decide it.
areas.wl: Jia Hao repeats Dad's words, so the lesson carries into the ending.

decoys.x1: A sleeping cat has no link to any memory.
decoys.x2: A crying baby is background noise, not a reminder.

stories.title: The Torn Poster
stories.text:
It was the last art lesson before the class display. [ha|The art room] smelled of paint and glue. Kai carried Mina's big poster to the wall. [x1|The fan in the corner whirred loudly.] His sleeve caught on a table. [hb|RRRIP!] The poster tore across the middle. Mina's face went pale. [hc|A roll of clear tape] sat on the shelf beside him. Kai's heart thumped.

He took a deep breath. [la|"I am so sorry, Mina," he said at once.] [x2|Other children kept painting.] [lc|He picked up the clear tape and fixed the poster carefully.] Mina was upset at first, but then she smiled. [lb|Kai felt his heart slow down and his shoulders relax.]

areas.memory: Last term in the art room, Kai spilled paint on a friend's drawing. He said sorry at once, and his friend forgave him.
areas.wh: The art room is the place where Kai spilled paint before.
areas.wr: Workable: a room is a broad hook. It only works because the memory happened in the same place.
areas.wl: Saying sorry at once is the same action as last term.

areas.memory: At home, Kai once ripped his school shirt and felt scared. Mum hugged him and said, "Accidents happen." He felt relieved.
areas.wh: The ripping sound is the same sound as his shirt tearing.
areas.wr: Good: a sound is a strong hook, but it comes at the exact moment of the accident, so a flashback would stop the action too soon.
areas.wl: Both times, Kai felt relieved once the worry eased.

areas.memory: Last year, Grandpa mended Kai's torn comic with clear tape. He said, "Broken things can be fixed."
areas.wh: Grandpa used the same kind of clear tape to mend Kai's comic.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object right where Kai must decide what to do. The memory shows him the answer.
areas.wl: Kai uses clear tape to mend the poster, just as Grandpa did.

decoys.x1: A fan is only noise. No memory connects to it.
decoys.x2: Other children painting is just the scene. It has no link to Kai's memories.

stories.title: The Lift Lobby
stories.text:
Mei stood in the lift lobby of her HDB block. She was late for tuition. [ha|The sharp smell of medicated oil] drifted from the corridor. [x1|A poster on the noticeboard asked people to recycle.] Old Mrs Lim shuffled in with two heavy bags. One was [hb|a green string bag with a broken handle.] [hc|The lobby was dim and quiet tonight.] Mei looked at her watch.

Mrs Lim's hands trembled, and she looked [lc|nervous about the stairs.] [x2|A pigeon sat on the railing outside.] Mei put down her bag. "[lb|No trouble at all!]" she said and smiled. [la|She picked up both bags and carried them to the door.] Mrs Lim patted her arm. Mei ran to tuition, a little late but happy.

areas.memory: Every Saturday, Mei carried Grandma's shopping bag home. Grandma always rubbed medicated oil on her sore knees.
areas.wh: Mrs Lim smells of the same medicated oil Grandma used.
areas.wr: Good: a smell is a strong hook, but the memory only says that Mei carries bags. It adds less than the string bag.
areas.wl: Carrying the bags is the same action Mei did for Grandma.

areas.memory: At the wet market, Grandma's green string bag broke and oranges rolled everywhere. A boy picked them up and said, "No trouble at all!"
areas.wh: The broken green string bag looks just like Grandma's bag.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object seen just as Mei must decide whether to help. The memory gives her the exact words.
areas.wl: Mei says the boy's words to Mrs Lim.

areas.memory: Once, the lights failed while Mei waited alone in a dim lobby. She felt nervous until a neighbour stayed with her.
areas.wh: A dim, quiet lobby is like the dim lobby when the lights failed.
areas.wr: Workable: dim lobbies are common, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Nervous is the same feeling for Mei then and Mrs Lim now.

decoys.x1: A recycling poster has nothing to do with Mei's memories.
decoys.x2: A pigeon is only part of the scene. No memory is connected to it.

stories.title: The Group Project
stories.text:
Jia Hao's group had one hour to make a model of the solar system. [ha|The silver floorball medal on his bag] caught the light. He grabbed the cardboard and the glue. [x1|The classroom clock ticked loudly.] "I will do it myself," he said. Mei and Ravi sat quietly. Ravi moved to [hb|the back corner of the room.] [hc|The snip of the scissors] was the only sound.

The planets were still not ready. [lb|Ravi looked left out and sad.] Jia Hao stopped. "[la|One player cannot win. A team can,]" he said. [x2|A bell rang in the corridor.] He gave Ravi the paint. [lc|He cut the cardboard while Mei did the gluing.] Soon the planets were done, and everyone cheered.

areas.memory: Last term, Jia Hao's floorball team won because he passed the ball to Ravi. Coach said, "One player cannot win. A team can."
areas.wh: Jia Hao won this medal with his floorball team.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object noticed just as he chooses to work alone. The memory gives him words that change his choice.
areas.wl: He says his coach's words aloud.

areas.memory: Once, Jia Hao refused to share his ideas with his team. He ended up alone in a corner, feeling left out.
areas.wh: The back corner is like the corner where Jia Hao once sat alone.
areas.wr: Workable: corners are common, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Left out is the same feeling Jia Hao once had, now seen in Ravi.

areas.memory: At home, Jia Hao and his sister made paper stars. She cut and he glued, and they finished early.
areas.wh: Cutting paper sounds like making paper stars at home.
areas.wr: Good: a sound is a strong hook, but the memory shows how to share jobs, not why it matters.
areas.wl: Splitting the jobs is the same action as with his sister.

decoys.x1: A ticking clock is only background noise.
decoys.x2: A bell in the corridor has no link to any memory.

stories.title: The Red Kite
stories.text:
Aisha's little brother Adam wanted to fly his kite. They went to the empty void deck. [ha|The open void deck] echoed with their footsteps. [x1|A neighbour's radio played softly upstairs.] Adam held [hb|a red kite with a snapped string.] Aisha sighed. "Hurry up!" she said. Adam's lip trembled. [hc|The paper flapped in the wind.]

Aisha took a breath. "[lb|Slow hands, kind hands,]" she whispered. [x2|A bicycle bell rang nearby.] She knelt down. [lc|She tied the string again and again until it held.] Adam's face relaxed, and [la|he felt safe with his big sister.] Soon the red kite rose high above the block.

areas.memory: When Aisha was five, Dad spent a whole afternoon at this void deck teaching her to tie her shoes. He never rushed her, and she felt safe.
areas.wh: This void deck is where Dad once taught Aisha patiently.
areas.wr: Workable: a void deck is a broad place, and the memory adds only a feeling.
areas.wl: Adam feels safe with Aisha, just as Aisha once felt safe with Dad.

areas.memory: Last year, Aisha's red kite lost its string. Grandpa fixed it slowly and said, "Slow hands, kind hands."
areas.wh: The snapped string is just like the one on Aisha's own red kite.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object seen just as Aisha is being unkind. The memory gives her the words to change.
areas.wl: She says Grandpa's words to herself.

areas.memory: Once, Mum tied and retied the string on Aisha's paper fan. She said, "Try again. I will wait."
areas.wh: The flapping paper sounds like Aisha's fan that Mum fixed.
areas.wr: Good: a sound is a strong hook, but it comes after Aisha has been unkind, and the memory shows only the action.
areas.wl: Tying the string again and again is the same action Mum did patiently.

decoys.x1: A radio upstairs is only background sound.
decoys.x2: A bicycle bell is a passing sound with no link to any memory.

stories.title: The Spelling Bee
stories.text:
Jun stood on the stage in the school hall for the spelling bee. He touched [ha|the small yellow ribbon on his shirt.] [x1|A girl in the front row waved a paper fan.] [hb|The stage was bright and hot.] "Spell necessary," said the teacher. Jun spelled it slowly. [hc|DING!] The bell rang. He had made a mistake.

Jun felt his eyes sting. [lb|His cheeks burned hot with embarrassment.] [x2|The teacher turned a page of her list.] [lc|He took a deep breath and blinked back his tears.] "[la|I was brave enough to try,]" he told himself. Then he clapped for the winner and smiled.

areas.memory: Grandma kept Jun's old Participant ribbon in a tin. She said, "The ribbon says, I was brave enough to try."
areas.wh: The yellow ribbon is just like Jun's old Participant ribbon.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object touched right before the problem. The memory gives him words that ease the loss.
areas.wl: He says Grandma's words to himself.

areas.memory: At his cousin's wedding, Jun sang on a bright stage and forgot the words. His cheeks burned hot with embarrassment.
areas.wh: The bright stage is like the stage where Jun forgot the words.
areas.wr: Workable: many stages are bright, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Burning cheeks and embarrassment match the wedding.

areas.memory: At the swimming gala, a bell rang and Jun came last. He took a deep breath and blinked back his tears.
areas.wh: The bell is the same sound as at the swimming gala.
areas.wr: Good: a sound is a strong hook, but it comes at the very moment of the mistake, so a flashback would stop the story too soon.
areas.wl: Taking a deep breath and blinking back tears is the same action.

decoys.x1: A girl with a paper fan is only part of the crowd.
decoys.x2: A teacher turning a page is not connected to any memory.

stories.title: The Free Peach
stories.text:
On Saturday, Kai went to the wet market with Grandpa. [ha|Grandpa's old straw hat] bobbed through the crowd. [x1|A fishmonger shouted the price of prawns.] The smell of [hb|sweet, ripe mangoes] filled the air. Kai walked down [hc|the wet, crowded aisle.] A vegetable auntie gave him a free peach. Kai took it quickly and walked on.

Grandpa stopped and raised his eyebrows. [x2|A trolley rattled past on the wet floor.] Kai remembered. "[la|Two small words can warm a big heart,]" he thought. [lb|He turned back, said thank you and smiled.] The auntie beamed. [lc|Kai felt proud and warm inside.]

areas.memory: Grandpa always wore his straw hat to the market. He taught Kai, "Two small words can warm a big heart: thank you."
areas.wh: Grandpa wore this same straw hat when he taught Kai about thank you.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object seen just when Kai forgets his manners. The memory gives him the exact words.
areas.wl: Kai thinks Grandpa's words, so the lesson carries into the ending.

areas.memory: Once, Grandpa bought Kai a ripe mango and waited. Kai turned to the seller, said thank you and smiled.
areas.wh: The smell of mangoes reminds Kai of the day he thanked the seller.
areas.wr: Good: a smell is a strong hook, and the memory shows what to do, but it does not say why it matters.
areas.wl: Turning back, thanking and smiling is the same action as at the mango stall.

areas.memory: At this market, Kai once helped carry a heavy bag. Grandpa praised him, and Kai felt proud and warm inside.
areas.wh: This crowded aisle is where Kai once helped Grandpa.
areas.wr: Workable: markets are crowded everywhere, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Kai feels proud and warm in both scenes.

decoys.x1: A fishmonger shouting prices is only noise.
decoys.x2: A trolley rattling past has no link to any memory.

stories.title: The Lantern Walk
stories.text:
Mei and her little cousin Zhi Xuan walked around the lake with their lanterns. [ha|The sweet smell of lotus mooncakes] floated from a stall. [x1|A band played near the stage.] Mei held her glowing red lantern high. They turned onto [hb|the dark path by the lake.] Suddenly Zhi Xuan's rabbit light went out. [hc|The small yellow torch in Mei's pocket] pressed against her leg. She hesitated.

Zhi Xuan's lip trembled, and [lb|his heart raced with fear.] [x2|Other children ran ahead, laughing.] Mei took out the torch. "[lc|Two lights are better than one,]" she said. [la|She stood close and shared her light with his rabbit.] Zhi Xuan smiled, and they walked on together.

areas.memory: Last Mid-Autumn, Mei saved half her mooncake for her cousin. Grandma said, "Sharing makes sweet things sweeter."
areas.wh: The mooncake smell is the same smell as at Grandma's table.
areas.wr: Good: a smell is a strong hook, but the memory is about sharing food, not light, so it fits less closely.
areas.wl: Sharing something she has is the same action, now with light.

areas.memory: Once, the path lights flickered while Mei walked alone. Her heart raced with fear until she reached the crowd.
areas.wh: A dark path is like the path where the lights flickered.
areas.wr: Workable: dark paths are common, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Fear is the same feeling for Mei then and Zhi Xuan now.

areas.memory: Last year, Mei's lantern went dark. An older girl shared her torch and said, "Two lights are better than one."
areas.wh: The yellow torch looks just like the one the older girl shared.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object right where Mei hesitates. The memory gives her the words and the answer.
areas.wl: Mei says the older girl's words to Zhi Xuan.

decoys.x1: A band playing is only background sound.
decoys.x2: Children running ahead have no link to any memory.

stories.title: The Promise
stories.text:
The day before Chinese New Year, Hui Min stood in the living room with Popo. She had promised to help clean the house. [ha|The sunny basketball court below] was full of her friends. [x1|A dog barked in the corridor.] Popo handed her [hb|a feather duster with a yellow handle.] Then Hui Min heard [hc|the happy bounce of a ball.] Her friends waved up at her.

Her tummy twisted, and she felt [la|guilty for even wanting to go.] [x2|The fan above the window creaked.] "[lb|A promise is like a knot. Keep it tight,]" she whispered. [lc|She leaned out and told her friends she would join them later.] Then she dusted every shelf with a smile.

areas.memory: Last year, Hui Min skipped helping Popo to play outside. Popo cleaned alone, and Hui Min felt guilty all evening.
areas.wh: The court is where Hui Min played instead of helping last year.
areas.wr: Workable: a court is a broad hook, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Guilt is the same feeling now as last year.

areas.memory: When Hui Min was six, Popo gave her a feather duster with a yellow handle. She said, "A promise is like a knot. Keep it tight."
areas.wh: Popo gave Hui Min a duster with this same yellow handle.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object in her hands just as she is tempted. The memory gives her the words that keep her promise.
areas.wl: She repeats Popo's words to herself.

areas.memory: Once, Hui Min told her friends she could not play because she had promised to help her brother. They waited, and she joined them later.
areas.wh: The bounce of the ball reminds her of the day she said no to her friends.
areas.wr: Good: a sound is a strong hook, but it comes after she is already tempted, and the memory shows only the action.
areas.wl: Telling her friends "later" is the same action as in the memory.

decoys.x1: A dog barking is only background noise.
decoys.x2: A creaking fan has no link to any memory.

stories.title: The Burnt Tarts
stories.text:
On the morning before Hari Raya, Farid decided to bake pineapple tarts alone. [ha|The smell of something burning] filled the air. [x1|A cheerful song played on the radio.] He pulled out the tray. The tarts were black. Farid held [hb|Mak's wooden spoon with the chipped handle] and stared at the mess. He stood in [hc|the small, hot kitchen,] and his shoulders dropped.

He felt [lc|stuck and frustrated.] [x2|A tap dripped into the sink.] "[lb|Many hands make light work,]" he said at last. He called, "Kak Aina, can you help me?" [la|He tipped the burnt tray into the bin and began again with a smile.] Soon the kitchen smelled sweet, and both of them were laughing.

areas.memory: Last year, Mak burnt a tray of cookies and only laughed. She tipped it into the bin and started again with a smile.
areas.wh: The burning smell is the same one from the burnt tray last year.
areas.wr: Good: a smell is a strong hook, but the memory shows how to restart, not why to ask for help.
areas.wl: Binning the tray and starting again is the same action Mak did.

areas.memory: Mak always let Farid stir with her wooden spoon. She said, "Many hands make light work."
areas.wh: The chipped spoon is the same one Mak let him stir with.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object in his hand just as he feels stuck. The memory gives him words that lead to asking for help.
areas.wl: Farid says Mak's words, and then asks Kak Aina.

areas.memory: In this same kitchen, Farid once got stuck on his homework and was too shy to ask for help. He felt stuck and frustrated for an hour.
areas.wh: This kitchen is where Farid once felt stuck.
areas.wr: Workable: a kitchen is a broad hook, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Stuck and frustrated is the same feeling in both scenes.

decoys.x1: A radio song is only background sound.
decoys.x2: A dripping tap has no link to any memory.

stories.title: The Smudged Rangoli
stories.text:
On Deepavali morning, Deepa knelt to finish her rangoli. [ha|Paati's tin of red powder with the dented lid] sat beside her. [x1|A string of fairy lights blinked above the door.] She sat on [hb|the front doorstep,] cool and bright in the sun. Then she heard [hc|the thud of running feet.] Her little brother Kumar dashed past and smudged the pattern.

Deepa's cheeks went hot. [x2|A neighbour called out a cheerful greeting.] [lc|She took a slow breath and knelt to redraw it with him.] "[la|Every flower has a few crooked petals,]" she told Kumar gently. [lb|She felt proud of the new flower they drew together.]

areas.memory: Paati taught Deepa rangoli with this tin. When a line went crooked, she said, "Every flower has a few crooked petals."
areas.wh: Paati's tin is the same one she used to teach Deepa.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object beside Deepa just before the problem. The memory gives her words that calm the moment.
areas.wl: She repeats Paati's words to Kumar.

areas.memory: Deepa once drew her first rangoli on this doorstep. Appa smiled, and she felt proud.
areas.wh: This is the doorstep where she drew her first rangoli.
areas.wr: Workable: a doorstep is a place hook, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Proud is the same feeling as at her first rangoli.

areas.memory: Last year, her cousin ran across her drawing. Deepa took a slow breath and helped him redraw it.
areas.wh: The thud of feet reminds her of her cousin running across the drawing.
areas.wr: Good: a sound is a strong hook and the memory shows what to do, but it comes at the very moment of the accident.
areas.wl: Breathing slowly and redrawing is the same action as last year.

decoys.x2: A neighbour's greeting has no link to any memory.

stories.title: The Parade Rehearsal
stories.text:
Jun Wei stood in line for the National Day parade rehearsal. [ha|The hot, empty field] shimmered in the sun. [x1|A teacher blew a whistle far away.] [hb|The steady beat of the drum] began. Jun Wei gripped the flag pole. [hc|His brother's old red cap] slipped over one eye. When the line turned, he stepped the wrong way and bumped his partner.

[la|His face felt hot with embarrassment.] [x2|A bird flew over the field.] He closed his eyes. [lb|He counted his steps under his breath until he found the beat.] "[lc|Everyone is looking at the flag, not at me,]" he told himself. He marched on with his chin up.

areas.memory: At his first practice in this field, Jun Wei marched the wrong way. His face burned with embarrassment.
areas.wh: This field is where Jun Wei marched the wrong way before.
areas.wr: Workable: a hot field is a broad place hook, and the memory only adds a feeling.
areas.wl: Embarrassment is the same feeling both times.

areas.memory: At home, Dad tapped a drum rhythm on the table. He taught Jun Wei to count his steps, one at a time.
areas.wh: The drum beat is like the rhythm Dad tapped on the table.
areas.wr: Good: a sound is a strong hook, but it begins before the mistake, so the flashback would come too early.
areas.wl: Counting steps is the same action Dad taught.

areas.memory: On his first day of practice, his big brother lent him a red cap. He said, "Everyone is looking at the flag, not at you."
areas.wh: The red cap is the very one his brother lent him.
areas.wr: Ideal: a personal object slipping over his eye just before he makes a mistake. The memory gives him the words he needs.
areas.wl: Jun Wei repeats his brother's words.

decoys.x1: A whistle far away is only background noise.
decoys.x2: A bird flying over has no link to any memory.
